blocks.text: Ladner Foreclosures & Court-Ordered Sales — Frequently Asked Questions

parts.t: How does a court-ordered sale work in Ladner, BC?

In British Columbia, when a borrower defaults on a mortgage, the lender petitions the BC Supreme Court for an Order Nisi and eventually an Order for Conduct of Sale. The property is listed on the MLS®, and any accepted offer Remains subject to BC Supreme Court approval.
What is Schedule A in a Ladner foreclosure offer?

Schedule A is the court-mandated addendum attached to the Contract of Purchase and Sale. It overrides standard warranties and stipulates that the property is sold strictly "as-is, where-is" on the possession date, with no Property Disclosure Statement from the seller.
Can other buyers submit competing bids at the court hearing?

Yes. Once the first accepted offer removes subjects, the lender schedules a BC Supreme Court hearing. Under Supreme Court Practice Direction 66, competing buyers may submit unconditional sealed bids (collected by 9:45 a.m. on the hearing morning), and the original buyer gets one chance to revise their offer.
Can I include financing and inspection subjects on the initial offer?

The first buyer whose offer is accepted by the conduct-of-sale holder can usually include standard due-diligence conditions (financing, home inspection, strata document review, and title check), which must be removed before the court approval hearing is booked.
What Ladner-specific checks should I do before bidding on a foreclosure?
Because court-ordered sales are "as-is," always inspect foundation settlement, drainage, Flood Construction Level compliance, municipal permits at the City of Delta, and — for
— two years of strata minutes and the depreciation report.
Why are there sometimes zero Ladner foreclosure listings showing?

Ladner is a low-turnover market with strong homeowner equity, so active court-ordered listings are rare at any given moment. When the live MLS® feed shows zero properties, it simply means no court-ordered sales are currently active in Ladner.
